name: ArrayList add, get, size
desc: Appends an element, reads one back by index, and returns the element count. Index access is constant time on the backing array.
body: Inserting or removing in the middle shifts the later elements, so that costs time proportional to the list size. `List.of(...)` returns an immutable list; wrap it in `new ArrayList<>(...)` before adding.

name: removeIf
desc: Removes every element that matches the predicate in one pass. Safe where a for-each loop with a remove call would throw ConcurrentModificationException.

name: List.sort
desc: Sorts the list in place with an external order. The sort is stable, so equal elements keep their input order.
body: `list.sort(null)` uses the natural order from `Comparable`. Put `reversed()` at the end when the whole chain should flip; put it on one key's comparator when only that key should.

name: List.of
desc: Builds a fixed size, immutable list in one line. Useful for seed data and test fixtures.

name: LinkedList ends
desc: Adds and removes at both ends in constant time. Index access walks the chain, so get(i) inside a loop is quadratic.
body: New code should prefer `ArrayDeque` for queue and stack work: one array, no node objects, and `null` is rejected so an empty poll is unambiguous. Keep `LinkedList` when you insert in the middle through a `ListIterator`.

name: HashMap put and get
desc: Stores a value under a key and reads it back. Average cost is constant; one null key and null values are allowed.
body: Iteration order follows the hash and changes after a resize, so never rely on it. A key class needs both `equals` and `hashCode`; a `record` supplies them.

name: getOrDefault
desc: Returns the stored value or the fallback when the key is missing. Removes a null check from counting code.

name: computeIfAbsent
desc: Creates the value on first use and returns it, which builds a map of lists without a null check.

name: merge
desc: Inserts the value when the key is new and combines it with the old value when it exists.

name: entrySet
desc: Iterates keys and values together without a second lookup. keySet() and values() cover the other two views.

name: TreeMap
desc: Keeps keys sorted at all times, by natural order or a comparator. Lookup and insert cost logarithmic time.
body: The navigable methods (`firstKey`, `lastKey`, `headMap`, `tailMap`, `floorKey`, `ceilingKey`) are the reason to pick it over a `HashMap` plus a sort. Natural ordering rejects a `null` key.

name: Sort map entries
desc: Sorts a copy of the entry set when the report order is by value. A map itself has no order to sort.
body: Add a tie breaker with `.thenComparing(Map.Entry.comparingByKey())`. For a map that stays sorted by value, keep a `TreeMap` keyed by the value instead, or sort on each print.

name: HashSet add
desc: Stores unique elements. Returns false when the element was already present, which makes duplicate detection a one liner.
example:
Set<String> guests = new HashSet<>();
boolean first = guests.add("anna@example.com");    // true
boolean again = guests.add("anna@example.com");    // false

System.out.println(guests.size());   // 1
System.out.println(guests.contains("anna@example.com"));   // true
body: The set uses `equals` and `hashCode`. A mutable field that feeds `hashCode` must not change while the object sits in the set, or lookups stop finding it.

name: TreeSet
desc: Keeps unique elements sorted. Deduplication uses compareTo or the comparator, not equals.

name: Queue offer and poll
desc: First in, first out. offer returns false when full, poll and peek return null when empty; add, remove, and element throw instead.

name: ArrayDeque
desc: Double ended queue for both FIFO lines and LIFO stacks. addFirst, addLast, pollFirst, pollLast, push, and pop cover both ends.
body: `ArrayDeque` rejects `null`, so a `null` from `poll` can only mean empty. It is faster than the legacy synchronized `Stack` for stack work.

name: Iterator remove
desc: Removes the element returned by the last next() call. The only legal way to delete while walking a fail-fast collection.
body: `removeIf` does the same job in one line. `ListIterator` adds `previous`, `set`, and `add` for editing during the walk.

name: Comparator.comparing
desc: Builds a multi key order outside the class. The first key decides, later keys break ties.
body: Use `comparingInt`, `comparingLong`, and `comparingDouble` for numbers to avoid boxing on each comparison. `nullsFirst` and `nullsLast` wrap a comparator for nullable fields. `Comparable` is the class's own order; a `Comparator` is an outside opinion and a class can have many.

name: filter, map, collect
desc: The three step pipeline: keep some rows, transform each row, store the result. Intermediate steps are lazy until the terminal call runs.
body: `toList()` returns an unmodifiable list, while `collect(Collectors.toList())` returns a mutable one in current JDKs. The source list is never changed by the pipeline.

name: mapToInt and sum
desc: Converts to a primitive stream, then totals it without boxing. Also unlocks average, min, max, and summaryStatistics.
body: `sum()` returns 0 for an empty stream. `average()` returns `OptionalDouble`, because an empty stream has no average.

name: groupingBy with counting
desc: Builds a map from key to number of rows. The plain one argument form gives key to List instead.
body: Without the map factory the result is a `HashMap`, so group order is arbitrary. A `null` key from the classifier throws `NullPointerException`.

name: summingInt
desc: Adds a numeric field per group, so one pass produces a map of totals.
example:
Map<String, Integer> revenueByCity = bookings.stream()
        .collect(Collectors.groupingBy(
                Booking::city,
                TreeMap::new,
                Collectors.summingInt(Booking::total)));

revenueByCity.forEach((city, total) ->
        System.out.printf("%-9s %6d%n", city, total));
body: Related downstreams: `summingLong`, `summingDouble`, `averagingInt`, and `summarizingInt`. Use them after grouping; `mapToInt` is no longer reachable at that point.

name: joining
desc: Joins stream elements into one string with a delimiter. No trailing comma, unlike a manual loop.
example:
String cities = bookings.stream()
        .map(Booking::city)
        .distinct()
        .sorted()
        .collect(Collectors.joining(", ", "[", "]"));

System.out.println(cities);   // [Budapest, Praha, Vienna]

name: toMap with merge
desc: Builds a map from stream elements. The merge function decides what happens when two rows share a key.
example:
Map<String, Integer> revenueByHotel = bookings.stream()
        .collect(Collectors.toMap(
                Booking::hotelName,
                Booking::total,
                Integer::sum,      // duplicates are added, not thrown
                TreeMap::new));

System.out.println(revenueByHotel);
body: Without the merge function a duplicate key throws `IllegalStateException: Duplicate key`. A fourth argument picks the map implementation, for example `TreeMap::new` for sorted keys.

name: flatMap
desc: Turns each element into a stream and joins the results, which flattens a field that holds a list.
example:
// Each booking holds the names of every guest on the reservation.
String everyone = bookings.stream()
        .flatMap(b -> b.guests().stream())
        .distinct()
        .sorted()
        .collect(Collectors.joining(", "));

System.out.println(everyone);   // Anna, Bela, Csilla, Dora
body: `map` would give a stream of lists here. Inside `collect`, `Collectors.flatMapping` does the same job as a downstream collector.

name: Optional map and orElse
desc: Transforms the value when present and supplies a fallback when empty, without a null check.
body: `orElse` evaluates its argument either way; use `orElseGet(() -> ...)` for anything expensive. Avoid `get()` without `isPresent()`, and avoid `Optional` as a field or parameter type.

name: sorted with a comparator
desc: Sorts the stream for the rest of the pipeline. A custom comparator is needed whenever the element is not Comparable or the order is not natural.

name: summaryStatistics
desc: Computes count, sum, min, max, and average in one pass over the data.
body: The collector form is `Collectors.summarizingInt`. On an empty stream the count and sum are 0 and the average is `0.0`, so guard the division if the report divides by the count.
